title: SOTA or Luck? The Winner's Curse in LLM Leaderboards
abstract: arXiv:2611.22227v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Public LLM leaderboards guide model evaluation and adoption, yet the reported performance of top-ranked models can be systematically overstated. This leaderboard winner's curse arises because ranking noisy benchmark scores rewards sampling luck alongside genuine ability. The same selection effect can distort scores throughout the leaderboard, a phenomenon we call the rank-induced bias. We develop an $m$-out-of-$N$ bootstrap to correct for this bias. It assumes a fixed model pool with independent, identically distributed bounded tasks while allowing arbitrary within-task correlation among models. Under exact population tiers separated by positive gaps, we prove that the bootstrap reduces $\Theta(N^{-1/2})$ ranking bias to expected residual bias $o(N^{-1/2})$. translated_abstract: 公共LLM排行榜指导着模型的评估与采用，然而排名靠前的模型所报告的性能可能被系统性高估。这种“排行榜赢家诅咒”源于对有噪声的基准测试分数进行排名时，会同时奖励采样运气和真实能力。同样的选择效应可能会扭曲整个排行榜上的分数，我们将这一现象称为“排名诱导偏差”。我们开发了一种m-out-of-N自助法（bootstrap）来纠正这种偏差。该方法假设模型池固定、任务独立同分布且有界，同时允许模型间在任务内存在任意相关性。在由正间隔分隔的精确总体层级下，我们证明了该自助法能将Θ(N^{-1/2})的排名偏差降低至期望残差偏差o(N^{-1/2})。在来自5个基准家族的14个基准测试上，排名第一模型的分数调整幅度约为0.09至3.86个百分点。在我们的SWE-bench Verified快照中，并列领先的模型
tldr: 该论文揭示了LLM排行榜中因排名噪声分数而产生的“赢家诅咒”与“排名诱导偏差”会系统性高估顶级模型的性能，并提出一种m-out-of-N自助法来纠正该偏差，在14个基准测试上排名第一模型的调整幅度为0.09至3.86个百分点。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals the "winner's curse" and "rank-induced bias" in LLM leaderboards, which systematically overstate top models' performance, and proposes an m-out-of-N bootstrap method to correct this bias, with rank-1 adjustments ranging from 0.09 to 3.86 percentage points across 14 benchmarks.
